title: Grace 'countdown' pip always draws '!', computed secs discarded
evidence:
secs := snap.grace_ticks_left * i32(v.catalogs.balance.logic_hz)
		_ = secs
		txt := fmt_bprintf(buf[:], "!", 0)
		draw_text(v, txt, {x + w + 8, y}, 18, p.state_critical)
detail: Comment says 'grace countdown pip' but it always draws '!'; secs is computed then discarded, and its multiply contradicts the divide used in the surge and forecast banners.
recommended_fix: Render the grace seconds (ticks / logic_hz, matching draw_surge_banner) instead of '!', or delete the dead secs line and the unused fmt_bprintf arg.

title: Right-click during router placement also cycles the pipe's QoS priority
detail: While placing a router, a right-click first cycles the pipe's QoS priority via the unconditional handler, and only then cancels placement; the cancel never swallows the side-effect.
recommended_fix: Guard the right-click pipe/node handler with `if app.placing < 0`, or move the placement-cancel check above it and return early.

title: synth_sting's descending_alarm parameter is never used
evidence: synth_sting :: proc(freqs: []f32, note_seconds: f32, descending_alarm: bool) -> rl.Sound {
detail: descending_alarm is declared in synth_sting's signature but never referenced in the body; both call sites pass true/false pointlessly.
recommended_fix: Drop the parameter and its two call-site arguments, or implement descending versus rising tone ordering if the flag was intended.

title: forecast_copy ignores its parameter and always returns a constant
detail: sp_name is ignored and forecast_copy always returns one literal; the per-provider parameter is dead and the call passes an empty string.
recommended_fix: Use sp_name to vary the copy, or remove the parameter and make forecast_copy a plain constant; update the forecast_copy("") call.

title: TICK_SECONDS constant is unused; comment falsely claims it is derived
evidence: TICK_SECONDS :: 0.1 // derived from balance.logic_hz at boot (catalog is the single source)
detail: TICK_SECONDS is a hardcoded 0.1 that is never referenced anywhere in the run package; the real tick length is computed separately as 1.0/logic_hz, so the comment is false.
recommended_fix: Delete the unused TICK_SECONDS constant, or actually use it as the default and correct the misleading 'derived' comment.

title: DATA_DIR constant is unused; load_catalogs uses its own parameter
evidence: DATA_DIR :: "../../data" // resolved at runtime from the executable's cwd in dev
detail: DATA_DIR is defined but load_catalogs uses its own data_dir parameter ('data'); the constant is unreferenced and its comment about runtime cwd resolution is inaccurate.
recommended_fix: Remove the unused DATA_DIR constant, or pass it as the default for the data_dir parameter if that path was intended.

title: App.autopilot_wired is a dead duplicate of Run_Context.autopilot_wired
detail: App.autopilot_wired is never initialized or read; autopilot_boot and autopilot_tick operate on Run_Context.autopilot_wired instead. The App-level field is a dead, never-made duplicate.
recommended_fix: Remove the autopilot_wired field from the App struct; Run_Context already owns and uses its own map.

title: App.press_valid is write-only (assigned but never read)
evidence:
press_valid: bool,
		app.press_valid = false
			app.press_valid = true
detail: press_valid is only ever assigned (false on press, true on a successful node snap) and never read anywhere in the app package.
recommended_fix: Remove the press_valid field and its two assignments, or read it where the press-valid distinction was actually intended.

title: load_hud_font uses ctprintf (not tprintf) on a runtime loop variable
evidence:
f := rl.LoadFontEx(fmt.ctprintf("%s", path), 64, nil, 400)
		path := fmt.tprintf("%s/%s", dir, name)
detail: load_hud_font uses fmt.ctprintf on a runtime loop variable, while catalogs.odin and cycle_priority use fmt.tprintf for the same kind of runtime formatting; the %s wrapper also just reproduces path.
recommended_fix: Use fmt.tprintf (or pass path directly) for consistency with the runtime string formatting used elsewhere; drop the ctprintf call.
